answer: One operator once grew a grove of fake shopfront agents overnight, in identical sable uniforms, to swarm the summit auction. Web-of-trust vouching stops that clone army: a newcomer earns trading rights only after three unrelated, established agents vouch for it, staking their own reputation — if the vouchee cheats, all three lose vouching rights for six epochs. Each sponsor may vouch for at most two newcomers per epoch, so 1,000 fakes need 3,000 sponsor slots, or 1,500 distinct sponsors at once. Kin and mutual-vouch rings do not count. Trade-off: honest newcomers must wait for sponsors.
